# File

<!-- gen:begin summary -->
<!-- Generated by `npm run generate:op-docs` from noodles-validate/registry.json. The title and the text between gen:begin and gen:end markers are replaced on every run; write anywhere else. -->

Read a CSV, JSON or Parquet file by URL. The relation is memoized: it is fetched once.
<!-- gen:end summary -->

## Syntax

<!-- gen:begin syntax -->
```json
{ "id": "n1", "op": "file", "name": "file", "x": 0, "y": 0, "params": {} }
```

One out of it starts at `"sourcePort": "out"`.
<!-- gen:end syntax -->

## Remarks

File reads one CSV, JSON or Parquet file into a table in DuckDB, in the engine worker. The table is read once and kept: a change downstream never reads the file again, and changing the URL, the format or a CSV option reads it anew.

A URL that starts with `@/` names a file in the project's data directory, so `@/data.csv` is the `data.csv` beside `noodles.json`. Any other URL is fetched by the browser, so a server on another domain has to allow cross-origin requests (CORS).

DuckDB detects each column's type from the file. The Header row, Column names and Null marker options apply to CSV only: turn Header row off and list Column names for a file whose first row is data. A JSON file is an array of objects, one row each.

To compute a value per row, add an [Attribute Create](./attribute.md) after it, or a [DuckDB SQL](./sql.md) node for anything a query does better.

## Examples

A CSV stored with the project, its positions made into a column for a layer:

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "n1", "op": "file", "name": "stations", "x": 0, "y": 0, "params": { "url": "@/stations.csv" } },
    { "id": "n2", "op": "attribute", "name": "position", "x": 300, "y": 0, "params": { "name": "position", "expression": "[lng, lat]" } }
  ],
  "edges": [{ "id": "e1", "source": "n1", "sourcePort": "out", "target": "n2", "targetPort": "in" }]
}
```
